description: Aura Phase-R = Phase 8 first slice — Subagent Dispatch Primitive. Wires the bridge between the existing internal/swarm package and chat.Hub via ChannelSwarm so the agent can spawn read-only fanout subagents via an LLM tool. Closes capability gap #5 'RunGraph subagent dispatch dinamico' from the 2026-05-16 'Aura come Claude Code' brainstorm. Scope is intentionally minimal: read-only fanout only (no write-capable workers, no team_collaboration, no plan-execute, no critic-review — those are full Phase 8 deferrals). Pattern carried over from Phase-K/L/M/N/O/P/Q: additive code only, tests lock the contract. Memory feedback_minipc_cpu_budget: max parallel children <= 3, no busy-loop polling. Reference docs in tree (canonical): prd.md §Phase 8 lines 1450-1494 (full RunGraph scope; this phase implements the read-only fanout first slice only). prd.md §5.4 channels/swarm (silent delivery + parent/child propagation). userStories.title: Add NodeSpec + SwarmHubBridge adapter (swarm.AgentTask -> chat.InboundMessage)
userStories.description: Pure adapter + types + tests; no consumer wiring in this story. (a) New file `internal/swarm/nodespec.go` with type `NodeSpec struct { Goal string; Instruction string; ToolAllowlist []string; MaxIterations int; MaxToolCalls int; BudgetSecs int; OutputSchema string (optional JSON schema); RiskTier string (read_only | write_proposal — only read_only valid in this slice); ParentRunID string; AssignmentID string }`. Validation function `Validate() error` rejects empty Goal, RiskTier != 'read_only', MaxIterations > 10, BudgetSecs > 300 (mini-PC budget memory). (b) New file `internal/swarm/hub_bridge.go` with `HubBridge struct` + factory `NewHubBridge(hub chat.Hub) *HubBridge`. Method `Dispatch(ctx context.Context, spec NodeSpec, principal identity.Principal) (childRunID string, err error)` — translates NodeSpec to chat.InboundMessage{Channel: ChannelSwarm, Mode: DeliveryModeSilent, Text: Goal, ChannelData: {parent_run_id, assignment_id, instruction, tool_allowlist, budgets}, PrincipalID: principal.ID}. Calls hub.ReceiveMessage and returns the resulting Run.ID. Does NOT wait — that's collection step (see US-R03). (c) NO change to existing swarm.Manager flow — this is an alternative entrypoint that will be wired in next stories. (d) Tests in `internal/swarm/hub_bridge_test.go`: 5 cases — NodeSpec validation rejects empty Goal; rejects RiskTier=write_proposal in this slice; Dispatch builds correct InboundMessage with Channel=Swarm; Dispatch passes parent_run_id through; budget > 300 rejected.

userStories.title: Wire ChannelSwarm in chat.Hub — silent run loop + result collection via Router.WaitForRun
userStories.description: Make ChannelSwarm an actual live channel in the hub. (a) Locate the hub's dispatch path in `internal/chat/hub.go` (existing ReceiveMessage already routes by Channel). Add (or verify presence of) the swarm-specific handling: when Channel=ChannelSwarm, the agent loop runs with the ChannelData-provided tool_allowlist + max_iterations + budget; output goes to a silent buffer (no Telegram, no web SSE), available via a new method `Router.WaitForRun(ctx, runID) (chat.Result, error)` with a context-bounded poll loop (poll every 200ms, max wait = BudgetSecs from ChannelData). (b) Implement `Router.WaitForRun` in `internal/chat/hub.go` (or a sibling file) that blocks until the run reaches a terminal state (Done/Error/Cancelled) and returns a chat.Result containing the final assistant text + tool_calls_count + tokens_total + elapsed_ms. Use existing chat.EventDone subscription pattern. (c) Capability inheritance check: when ChannelSwarm receives a run, verify the principal's grants include CapabilityToolExecute + capability for each tool in tool_allowlist. Deny with chat.EventError on failure. Use the existing identity.Authorize boundary. (d) Tests in `internal/chat/hub_swarm_test.go`: 4 cases — ChannelSwarm dispatches the run + run completes silent; WaitForRun blocks until done; tool_allowlist outside parent grant is denied; budget exceeded triggers cancellation+terminal failed event.

userStories.title: Add subagent_dispatch LLM tool (spawn + wait + collect with parallel fanout)
userStories.description:
Expose the subagent primitive to the LLM as an action-dispatch tool. (a) New file `internal/agent/tools/registry/subagent.go` with `SubagentDispatchTool` struct + Definition + Execute. Schema uses ActionDispatchOneOf (Phase-L pattern): actions are 'spawn' (parallel fanout: array of NodeSpec → returns array of child_run_ids) and 'collect' (array of child_run_ids → blocks until all done, returns aggregated results). Description copy: 'Spawn up to 3 read-only subagents in parallel and collect their results. Each child runs in isolation with its own context window, tool allowlist (subset of yours), and budget. Cannot perform write operations (wiki_page write, source store, task schedule etc. — all blocked). Returns concise summaries on collect. Use for: parallel web search across topics, multi-source synthesis, divergent reasoning paths.' Per-action required: spawn: nodes (array of {goal, instruction (opt), tool_allowlist (opt, defaults to read-only set), budget_secs (opt, default 60)}); collect: child_run_ids (array). (b) Spawn: validate len(nodes) <= 3 (mini-PC budget); for each node, create NodeSpec with RiskTier='read_only'; call HubBridge.Dispatch in parallel via errgroup; return the child_run_ids array as JSON. (c) Collect: for each child_run_id, call Router.WaitForRun (parallel via errgroup, each bounded by node's budget); aggregate results in a markdown structured output: '## Subagent <i>: <goal_summary>

<reply_text>

Tokens: N | Tool calls: M | Elapsed: T ms
'. (d) Register in registry.go alongside agent_note, recall_user_memory, recall_operational. (e) Tests in `internal/agent/tools/registry/subagent_test.go`: 5 cases — spawn 1 node returns 1 child_run_id; spawn 3 nodes parallel; spawn 4 nodes rejected (cap 3); collect 1 child returns result; collect mixed (1 success + 1 timeout) returns partial with error annotation per failed slot.
